title: October Surprise in Michigan: Rep. Haley Stevens Endorses Republican Mike Rogers for Senate
snippet: In an extraordinary late-race twist, Democratic Congresswoman Haley Stevens has endorsed Republican Mike Rogers over her former primary opponent, Democrat Abdul El-Sayed, threatening party unity in a crucial Senate battleground.
content:
DETROIT — In a shocking late-race turn of events that sent political shockwaves through Michigan and Capitol Hill, Democratic U.S. Rep. Haley Stevens endorsed Republican candidate Mike Rogers for the U.S. Senate on Sunday, just two days before voters head to the polls.

The high-stakes move came after weeks of escalating tension following a bitter August Democratic primary in which Abdul El-Sayed narrowly defeated Stevens. The endorsement led to immediate blowback within her own party, prompting her top legislative aide to resign in protest and drawing swift condemnation from Democratic leadership.

A Fractured Front on the Eve of the Election

The intraparty drama came to a head Sunday morning in Detroit. Stevens was initially slated to attend a unity church service alongside El-Sayed and prominent Democrats, including South Carolina Rep. Jim Clyburn and Michigan Rep. Debbie Dingell. However, after being asked not to attend due to growing distractions surrounding her friction with the El-Sayed campaign, Stevens instead attended a nearby worship service at Perfecting Church alongside Rogers and his wife.

"Our Democratic nominee for Senate said I was no longer welcome in his campaign and that I should stay away," Stevens announced in a video releasing her endorsement. "And he’s right. And that’s why I am endorsing Mike Rogers for the United States Senate today."

Standing beside Rogers after the service, Stevens maintained she wasn't abandoning her party overall. "I’m not turning my back on Democrats," she told reporters. "It is this one vote."

Swift Backlash and GOP Applause

The backlash from Democrats was immediate and scathing. Senate Majority Leader Chuck Schumer labeled the endorsement a "despicable betrayal," while Michigan Democratic Party Chair Curtis Hertel declared that Stevens had abandoned her core values, stating she would no longer be considered a member of the state party moving forward. Stevens’ chief of staff resigned shortly after the announcement, expressing heartbreak over the decision.

El-Sayed sought to downplay the fallout when questioned by reporters, framing his campaign's focus strictly on working-class economic concerns. "At the end of the day, I actually don’t think about Haley Stevens," El-Sayed said. "None of this matters."

Meanwhile, Republicans seized on the rift in the key swing state. Former President Donald Trump took to social media to commend Stevens for showing "unprecedented loyalty" to Michigan voters, while House Speaker Mike Johnson praised her willingness to speak out.

With Michigan’s open Senate seat—currently held by retiring Democrat Gary Peters—vital to determining control of the chamber, the last-minute fallout leaves Democrats scrambling to consolidate voters in Detroit and its surrounding suburbs ahead of Tuesday’s pivotal vote.
